# openclatura

> Turns a SMILES string into its IUPAC name with deterministic Blue Book rules (no LLM in the loop), and explains how the name is built. The drawing editor at https://openclatura.org is for people; agents should use the plain-text URLs below.

## Name a molecule

    GET https://openclatura.org/smiles=<SMILES>

Example: https://openclatura.org/smiles=CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1

    smiles: CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1
    name: N-phenylacetamide
    opsin: matched

- `smiles:` is the SMILES the server received. Check that it is the one you sent (see Encoding).
- `opsin:` is an independent check: OPSIN, a separate name-to-structure parser, reads the name back. `matched` means the name gives back the same molecule. Other values: `mismatched` (OPSIN read a different molecule), `name_unparseable` (OPSIN could not read the name), `error`, and `skipped_no_java` / `skipped_no_opsin` (the check could not run).
- On failure the second line is `error: <reason>` and the status is 422.

## Describe how the name is built

    GET https://openclatura.org/describe=<SMILES>

Example: https://openclatura.org/describe=CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1

Returns a plain-text description: the principal characteristic group, the parent skeleton and its numbering, each substituent, and the IUPAC Blue Book rules applied (P-numbers). This is the output of `openclatura describe`.

## Encoding

Percent-encode the SMILES, e.g. `encodeURIComponent(smiles)` or `urllib.parse.quote(smiles, safe="")`. If you write the URL by hand, at least:

- `#` → `%23`. An unescaped `#` ends the URL: `CC#N` is read as `CC` and named ethane.
- `%` → `%25` (two-digit ring closures such as `C%10`).
- `\` → `%5C`. Browsers and many HTTP clients turn an unescaped `\` in a path into `/`, which flips double-bond stereo (`F/C=C\F` becomes `F/C=C/F`).

`+` can be sent as-is; it is always read as `+`, never as a space.

If you cannot control encoding, put the SMILES in the query string, where `\` survives:

    GET https://openclatura.org/name?smiles=<SMILES>
    GET https://openclatura.org/describe?smiles=<SMILES>

## Options

Add these to the query string of any URL above, e.g. `/smiles=CCO?format=json` or `/name?smiles=CCO&verify=0`.

- `format=json`: JSON instead of text. For names: `{"ok", "smiles", "name", "error", "rules_hit", "rule_hints", "opsin_check": {"status", ...}}`. For descriptions: `{"smiles", "name", "summary", "paragraphs", "rules_hit", ...}`.
- `verify=0`: skip the OPSIN check (it is on by default, as in the command-line tool).
- `no_cache=1`: do not store the structure in the site's result cache. The cache only makes repeat requests fast; structures are not shared or used for training.

## Status codes

- 200: named or described.
- 400: no SMILES given; the body is a short usage note.
- 422: not a valid SMILES, or not nameable by the current rules; the body says which.
- 429: rate limit reached; wait for the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header.

## Limits

At most 10 molecules per second from one IP address. Ask for one molecule per request and pace your requests.

For large sets, run openclatura locally: `pip install openclatura`, then `openclatura name "<SMILES>"` or `openclatura batch smiles.txt` (one SMILES per line, JSON Lines out). The OPSIN check needs Java; add `--no-verify` without it.
